summary: Hull Mountain lookout (Mendocino NF): 1974 hexagonal ground cabin replaced an earlier R1 cabin; destroyed by fire on an unknown date; no current site description found.

facts.design: Single-story hexagonal ground cabin with flying buttress supports, designed by USFS Architect Robert Sandusky
facts.status_note: Register says the 1974 cabin was destroyed in a fire at an unknown date; removal listed as unknown (burned)
facts.agency: US Forest Service - Mendocino National Forest

access.note: On Mendocino National Forest land per the register; no closure is described, but no route or current access is described in the sources read

events.note: Lookout Charles Henry at the summit station, as described in a September 6, 1940 newspaper item
Lightning fire north of San Hedrin that a crew could not locate; the lookout guided them to it by radio (annual report of November 8, 1940)
Single-story hexagonal ground cabin with flying buttress supports
The 1974 lookout replaced an earlier R1 ground cabin; the earlier cabin's date is not given
Registered February 2, 2020 as FFLOS US 1908, CA 103; nominated by Brad Eells

notes_for_editor: Two sources only. Build and registration dates match the brief. No source read describes the site today; the register's 2009 photo is listed but not described in its text. Access 'public' is inferred from national forest land, not a stated policy. A geocaching listing (geocache GCKDB7) claims an original 1930s CCC lookout, but the page did not return readable text and it is not cited. Date of the destruction fire is unknown.
